question: Does the directional gap track robot-base orientation when the object layout remains fixed in world coordinates?

design.selection_rule: Select the first candidate for which negative-yaw, zero-yaw, and positive-yaw layouts all pass every model-blind feasibility row; otherwise fail closed.

exact_prompts.left: Put the Rubik's cube to the left of the bowl.
exact_prompts.right: Put the Rubik's cube to the right of the bowl.

held_fixed_in_world_coordinates: rubiks_cube, bowl, and banana full poses
all camera world poses and intrinsics
held_fixed_across_cells: success predicate and requested 45-degree cone definition in the registered robot frame
static prompt bytes, controller, action cap, checkpoint, preprocessing, and renderer
environment and sampling seed within each six-cell matched block

requirements: fresh reset for every arm and direction
no requested predicate true at reset
collision-free settled scene and robot configuration
target and reference reachable under the frozen controller limits
nonblank required camera views and persistent viewport write
LEFT and RIGHT physical fingerprints equal within each yaw arm
model_blind_gate.failure_rule: If no preregistered absolute yaw passes symmetrically, V3-B006 fails closed; do not invent a smaller angle.

analysis_plan.primary: Within each seed and yaw arm, compute signed endpoint redirection and requested-side-depth contrasts; estimate the direction-by-signed-yaw interaction.
analysis_plan.secondary: Report the arm-by-direction binary success table, per-seed paired contrasts, exact sign tests, and failure taxonomy.
analysis_plan.claim_boundary: Rotating only the base changes embodiment-to-scene geometry and visible robot pose; it is not a pure training-data intervention.

release_boundary.next_action: Run the exact zero-model-request symmetric yaw feasibility gate and freeze its numeric output and hashes in a new release amendment.
